ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: There is a “swallowing and spitting” relationship between a tributary of a certain large river and the main stream. The figure below shows the annual net runoff (the difference between output runoff and input runoff) and annual net sediment transport (the difference between output sediment amount and input sediment amount) at the outlet of this tributary from 1970 to 2000. <image1> Since 1983, the annual net sediment transport has generally shown a downward trend. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The legend shows that the dashed line represents “annual net sediment transport volume,” the dotted line represents “annual net runoff volume,” and the horizontal solid lines represent the multi-year average values of the two. Observing the dashed line, it can be seen that after 1983, although there are fluctuations, its overall position tends to decrease, indicating that the annual net sediment transport volume generally shows a downward trend. Reasoning: A decrease in annual net sediment transport volume indicates that the net output of sediment from this tributary basin to the river channel has decreased. A decrease in sediment usually means that soil and water loss in the basin has been reduced; vegetation improvement can intercept precipitation, consolidate soil and protect slopes, thereby reducing sediment entering the river. Therefore, this change most likely indicates that the vegetation coverage condition in this tributary basin has improved, especially that the forest coverage rate has increased.

raw_record.question_text:
There is a “swallowing and spitting” relationship between a tributary of a certain large river and the main stream. The figure below shows the annual net runoff (the difference between output runoff and input runoff) and annual net sediment transport (the difference between output sediment amount and input sediment amount) at the outlet of this tributary from 1970 to 2000.

<image1>

Since 1983, the annual net sediment transport has generally shown a downward trend. What change in the vegetation condition of this tributary basin does this change most likely indicate?

method.method_draft: 根据题干要求关注1983年以来的年净输沙量。先从图中确认虚线代表年净输沙量，并判断其1983年后总体下降。再把“净输沙量下降”解释为支流流域向河道输送的泥沙减少。结合地理常识，泥沙减少最可能是水土流失减轻，而植被状况改善会减轻水土流失。因此回答：该支流流域森林覆盖率提高。
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图例显示，虚线表示“年净输沙量”，点线表示“年净径流量”，水平实线表示二者多年平均值。观察虚线可见，1983年以后虽有波动，但总体位置趋于降低，说明年净输沙量总体呈下降趋势。
推理：年净输沙量下降，表示该支流流域向河道净输出的泥沙减少。泥沙减少通常意味着流域水土流失减轻；植被改善能够拦截降水、固土护坡，从而减少泥沙入河。因此，这一变化最可能说明该支流流域植被覆盖状况改善，尤其是森林覆盖率提高。

method.method_draft: 从图像中同时比较1983年后的年净径流量和年净输沙量：净输沙量总体走低，但净径流量并没有相应持续走低。由此推断该流域的水沙关系发生改变，即单位径流携带泥沙减少或泥沙供给减少。题目要求从植被状况解释这种变化，因此用植被保持水土的知识判断：植被变好，具体表现为森林覆盖率提高。
method.CoT_raw:

推理：净输沙量下降而净径流量未同步持续下降，说明水沙关系发生变化，即单位径流携带的泥沙减少，或流域泥沙供给减少。若从植被状况解释，植被改善会增强涵养水源、保持水土能力，减少土壤侵蚀和泥沙入河。因此最可能说明该支流流域森林覆盖率提高。

raw_record.original_question:
某大河的一条支流与干流之间存在“吞吐”关系。下图示意该支流出口处1970—2000年间年净径流量（输出径流量与输入径流之差）和年净输沙量（输出泥沙量与输入泥沙量之差）。

<image1>

1983年以来，年净输沙量总体呈下降趋势。这一变化最可能说明该支流流域植被状况发生了什么变化？
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The legend shows that the dashed line represents “annual net sediment transport volume,” the dotted line represents “annual net runoff volume,” and the horizontal solid lines represent the multi-year average values of the two. Observing the dashed line, it can be seen that after 1983, although there are fluctuations, its overall position tends to decrease, indicating that the annual net sediment transport volume generally shows a downward trend.
Reasoning: A decrease in annual net sediment transport volume indicates that the net output of sediment from this tributary basin to the river channel has decreased. A decrease in sediment usually means that soil and water loss in the basin has been reduced; vegetation improvement can intercept precipitation, consolidate soil and protect slopes, thereby reducing sediment entering the river. Therefore, this change most likely indicates that the vegetation coverage condition in this tributary basin has improved, especially that the forest coverage rate has increased.
